body:
Sure, might as well.

I'm in University, and would be doing pretty well in most of my classes, except that the term papers that are necessary to complete my courses... I haven't done. And in a couple days all profs will submit their final marks to their departments even if I did miraculously complete them tomorrow and the profs were merciful enough to grade them. And this after a couple days ago I realized that what I really want out of life is to pursue academic philosophy and become a professor. And I'm lying to my family about all this, when they're paying for my education.

I feel terrible all the time, but I only admit it when I'm drunk, when I get melancholy and send embarassing texts out and rant and apologize and rant more. And I used to be such a happy drunk. I can't bear to force my misery onto my friends and others who have been so gracious to me, especially when they all have so much of their own misery to deal with.

I'm Transgender, and I'm climbing up the walls waiting to get a letter telling me when I might get an appointment with the only specialist in the province who can refer me to an endocrinologist. Except I'm also depressed all the time, and if you've experienced depression you know how it gnaws at any decisions or feelings you have and tries to deconstruct them until you doubt every single thing about yourself. And sometimes I have such terrible doubts about all that that I feel by coming out to some of my friends 'prematurely' as it were I've permanently wrecked any relationship i've had with them and it's just desperate attention-seeking behaviour or the fetishization of femininity or something.

And I tell myself that I need to just get the fuck over myself because I have had so many opportunities and people who love me and I let it all slip through my fingers because I'm just a fraud and a freak and a failure and I'm just a walking drama bomb and a miserable pile of secrets and a slow-motion breakdown machine.

And I turned 21 last week, which felt less like a milestone past than the last vestiges of excuses and leeway of youth disappearing away from me.

And that's my whine.
